claims.text: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and the selected equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets can be prepared as single-phase FCC alloys by standard thermomechanical processing.
The target Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloys and their subsets exhibit differing degrees of local chemical ordering or clustering.
Differences in local chemical ordering or clustering govern differences in deformation and failure behavior among the target alloys.
Increasing short-range order creates a more heterogeneous local energy landscape.
The ordering-induced local energy landscape raises barriers to dislocation glide and enhances dislocation pinning.
Enhanced dislocation pinning increases yield strength.
Enhanced local ordering modifies, and typically increases, strain hardening.
Annealing at approximately 600–750 °C for 15 minutes to several hours, followed by rapid quenching, can systematically adjust short-range ordering or clustering.
The proposed annealing and quenching treatments can alter ordering without causing macroscopic phase separation, gross segregation, or secondary-phase formation.
Atom probe tomography can quantify cluster size, species distributions, and the degree of short-range chemical order in these alloys.
X-ray diffuse scattering can provide an independent estimate of ordering parameters.
High-resolution TEM, including the proposed use of controlled doping markers, can independently verify local ordering while excluding major segregation.
Alloys engineered to have more local chemical order than the conventionally processed equiatomic quinary baseline will have higher yield strength.
Excessive ordering can induce stress concentrations and stress localization.
Stress localization caused by excessive ordering can reduce ductility.

The proposed relationship is limited to single-phase FCC samples in which ordering is the primary microstructural variable and is not expected to apply after phase separation, gross segregation, or secondary-phase formation.
